question: Should lithium-ion batteries carry a refundable deposit, like the one many US states put on car batteries?
answer: Deposits make waste worth collecting. Car batteries come back at about 99% in the US, where retailers add a charge refunded when the old one is returned. Lithium cells have no such pull: thrown into household bins, they are crushed in lorries and start fires. A deposit makes each one worth picking up.
move: Whichever side you took, ask whether deposits or scrap value drive returns.
counterpoint: Car batteries come back because the lead is worth money: scrap dealers pay for old ones, deposit or not. Most lithium cells are small and sealed inside phones, earbuds and vapes, so a deposit on each is hard to charge and harder to refund. Drop-off points, shop take-back and bans like the UK's on disposable vapes do more for less.
source: Battery Council International, recycling rate study, 2019
reference: Battery Council International, National Recycling Rate Study, 2019
